title: Was There a Port off Poompuhar 15,000 Years Ago?
excerpt: Sonar surveys have revealed harbour-like forms beneath the Bay of Bengal, but the claim that they are a 15,000-year-old port remains unproven.

thumbnail.alt: Fishing boats drawn up on the broad sandy beach at Poompuhar on the Bay of Bengal

title: Attirampakkam’s Million-Year-Old Stone Tools
excerpt: Acheulean handaxes buried near Chennai show that tool-making hominins lived in southern India at least 1.07 million years ago—and probably much earlier.

thumbnail.alt: Historical illustration showing several Acheulean handaxe forms

title: Attirampakkam’s 385,000-Year-Old Technological Transition
excerpt: A younger layer at Attirampakkam records the decline of Acheulean handaxes and an early Middle Palaeolithic toolkit beginning around 385,000 years ago.

thumbnail.alt: A selection of small pointed and flaked stone tools from Attirampakkam
